title: Mary Kay: A Leader in the Beauty Product Industry

source.name: VOA Learning English — Mary Kay: A Leader in the Beauty Product Industry
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: One woman started the business in the 1960s with an investment of $5,000.
Mary Kathlyn Wagner was born in the state of Texas in 1918. For much of her childhood, she cared for her sick father while her mother worked long hours at a restaurant.

Mary Kay married Ben Rogers when she was 17 years old. They had three children before he left home to serve in World War Two. When he returned, their marriage ended. Mary Kay looked for a job so she could support her children.

She began selling different kinds of products. One night, Mary Kay was showing products at the home of Ova Heath Spoonemore. Ms. Spoonemore began giving her guests some homemade skin care products. The products were developed by her father, J.W. Heath, in Arkansas. Mary Kay tried the skin care products and liked them.

She bought the rights to Heath’s skin care products and started her own company. She paid $500 for the legal rights to the products. And in 1963, The Mary Kay Cosmetics company began operating in Dallas, Texas.
The idea was to sell skin care products through demonstrations in homes and offices. Independent sales representatives bought beauty products from the company and sold them at higher prices.

Mary Kay decided that each representative who brought other saleswomen into the company would receive part of the new person’s earnings. That way, experienced sales representatives would be willing to train new ones.
By 1965, the company was selling almost one million dollars in products.
Mary Kay Cosmetics became one of the most successful direct sellers of skin care products in America. It continues to have sales offices and representatives in many different countries.

Mary Kay aimed to grow sales based on the idea that it is best to compete against yourself. That means every individual is trying to beat their own sales records. Prizes for high sales marks included special paid holidays and jewelry. Until a few years ago, a pink Cadillac was a top prize.

Later, she started the Mary Kay Ash Charitable Foundation, a nonprofit group that provides money to support research on cancers affecting women. In 2001, the company and foundation expanded their goals to help prevent violence against women.
Mary Kay Ash also wrote three books. She worked in her business until she suffered a stroke in 1996. She died in 2001.
Sales representatives say Mary Kay developed a way for women to earn money and still spend time with their families.

questions.q: What does the text suggest about Mary Kay’s early life?
options: She grew up in a wealthy family that owned a restaurant in Texas
She left her home state as a teenager to study business
She had family duties to carry out while still a child
She trained as a beautician before she was old enough to marry
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: bà chăm cha bị bệnh trong khi mẹ làm việc nhiều giờ ở nhà hàng → phải gánh trách nhiệm gia đình từ nhỏ.

questions.q: Why did Mary Kay begin looking for work?
options: Her husband had asked her to help him to run his business after the war
She had to support her children by herself after her marriage ended
She had just finished her studies and was looking for a career
She wanted to open a restaurant of her own like the one her mother worked in
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: sau khi hôn nhân kết thúc “Mary Kay looked for a job so she could support her children”.

questions.q: How did Mary Kay come to sell the skin care products that made her company?
options: She liked some homemade creams shown at a party and then paid to own the formulas
She copied the recipe from a magazine and tested it on her friends
She inherited the products from the woman who had invited her to the party
She invented the formula herself while she was looking after her sick father
questions.explain: Đoạn 4–5: bà dùng thử sản phẩm tự làm tại buổi giới thiệu, thích nó rồi “bought the rights … for $500” và lập công ty.

questions.q: How did the independent sales representatives earn their money?
options: They were paid a fixed monthly salary directly by the company
They received a share of the founder’s own personal earnings
They charged customers a fee for coming to each demonstration
They resold the company’s goods to customers at a higher price
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: đại diện độc lập mua sản phẩm của công ty rồi bán lại “at higher prices”.

questions.q: Why did Mary Kay let representatives share in the earnings of the people they brought in?
options: So that the company could spend much less money on advertising
So that representatives would not leave to join competing firms
So that new recruits would pay for their own training courses
So that experienced sellers would have a reason to teach the newcomers
questions.explain: Đoạn 7: “That way, experienced sales representatives would be willing to train new ones.”

questions.q: What does “compete against yourself” mean in the context of the company’s sales idea?
options: Teams of sellers compete against their own managers for prizes
Each seller must try to win customers away from a rival company
Each person tries to improve on their own earlier sales figures
Sellers are asked to sell fewer products than they sold the year before
questions.explain: Đoạn 10: “every individual is trying to beat their own sales records” ≈ cố vượt thành tích bán hàng trước đó của chính mình.

questions.q: By the middle of the 1960s the company was already selling products worth nearly a million dollars.
questions.explain: Đoạn 8: “By 1965, the company was selling almost one million dollars in products.”

questions.q: Mary Kay Ash received a literary prize for one of her books.
questions.explain: Đoạn 12 chỉ nói bà viết ba cuốn sách; không nói về giải thưởng.
